title.narrative: Strengthened knowledge and capacity of constituents to promote gender equality and equal opportunities and treatment for all in the world of work

description.narrative:
Gender inequality and discrimination in the world of work continue to pose significant challenges in Tanzania. In response, the ILO is collaborating with national stakeholders to strengthen the country’s efforts in promoting gender equality, equal treatment, and opportunities for all workers. This programme aims to address gender-based violence and harassment, support the professionalization of domestic work, and improve social protection and legal frameworks to enhance workplace inclusivity and safety.
The intervention focuses on marginalized groups, including women, youth, domestic workers, persons with disabilities, and people living with HIV. It works to ensure their access to decent work opportunities through capacity building, policy reforms, and the development of gender-responsive guidelines. The programme promotes decent work in the care economy and fosters investments in gender-sensitive care policies and systems.
The ILO’s strategy includes policy advice, capacity building for key stakeholders, and advocacy for the adoption and implementation of international labor standards, such as ILO Conventions C190 and C189. By strengthening institutions, providing technical support, and improving social dialogue, the programme contributes to Tanzania’s broader goals of achieving gender equality (SDG 5), promoting decent work and economic growth (SDG 8), and reducing inequalities (SDG 10). Through these efforts, the ILO supports Tanzania in fostering a more inclusive, fair, and safe labor market for all.
